sentences.text: Liaoningvenator was a small troodontid with an estimated total body length of approximately 69 centimeters.
This dinosaur possessed a long, narrow, and triangular skull measuring 9.8 centimeters in length.
Its spine consisted of ten cervical vertebrae, twelve dorsal vertebrae, and at least sixteen caudal vertebrae.
Compared to its close relatives, Liaoningvenator had relatively long legs, particularly the femur, and the deltopectoral crest on the humerus extended for 40% of the bone's length.
The specimen was found in the Lujiatun Beds of the Yixian Formation in Shangyuan, Beipiao, Liaoning, China, a site shared with other Chinese troodontids.
Shen Cai-Zhi and colleagues named the species Liaoningvenator curriei in 2017 based on an articulated and nearly complete skeleton.
The genus Liaoningvenator was formally named by Shen et al. in 2017.
Evidence from the tibia suggests that Liaoningvenator's growth slowed substantially by the end of its third year.
The absence of an external fundamental system (EFS) on the tibia indicates that the holotype was still growing when it died.
The presence of avascular bone in outer layers and evidence of bone remodeling suggest the holotype was nearing skeletal maturity.
Liaoningvenator's skeleton had an exceptional posture with its head curved forward and limbs tucked, differing from the classic death pose or sleeping posture seen in Mei and Sinornithoides.
Shen and colleagues identified traits that placed Liaoningvenator within the family Troodontidae, including the pneumatic opening on the rear of the quadrate and the oval shape of the foramen magnum.
Within the Troodontidae, the closest relative of Liaoningvenator was Eosinopteryx, and it was also closely related to Anchiornis and Xiaotingia.
The grouping of Liaoningvenator with Anchiornis and Xiaotingia offered evidence against their traditional placement as non-troodontid members of the Paraves.
Liaoningvenator belongs to the subfamily Jinfengopteryginae.
Liaoningvenator lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 126 million years ago.
The Lujiatun beds consist of fluvial and volcanic deposits, indicating a landscape of rivers and volcanoes that may have killed the animals via lahars.

It is debated whether the shared traits like flattened recurved teeth, a folded acromion edge, and a backward-projecting pubis definitively unite Liaoningvenator with Anchiornis and Xiaotingia against other hypotheses.
